title: GPU falls off the bus: escalate, repair, burn in, return
teaches: A health check can find hardware faults; those must not auto-resume after repair. Take the drain away from NHC, repair, burn in behind a reservation, then return.

got.summary: Hardware fault found by the health check (NHC). Keep it out of service; NHC would resume it as soon as its check passes, so take the drain over before the repair.

commands: scontrol update nodename=slurm-c1 state=drain reason="triage: hardware: <ticket>"   # NHC never resumes a drain it didn't set
sbatch -p burnin -w slurm-c1 --gres=gpu:4 --exclusive -J burnin -o /var/tmp/burnin-%j.out --wrap /usr/local/sbin/lab-burnin   # after repair
evidence: state IDLE+DRAIN; CPUs 0/2 allocated; GRES gpu:fake:4 (in use: gpu:fake:0(IDX:N/A))
reason "NHC: check_gpu_count:  GPU missing: 3 of 4 devices present" set 2s ago by root
next_steps: Keep the node drained; don't resume it until the hardware is fixed.
Open a hardware ticket with the reason text and node serial; on real GPUs, pull `nvidia-smi -q` and dmesg Xid lines first.
After repair, run a burn-in job in the burnin partition before returning it to batch.
